input: Scheduled ventures brief (continue work on the repo: develop, deploy, market, sell and support revenue-generating products; merge when done)
task: Deepen (flagship 7) photo-editing: Bayer per-pixel Laplacian weight

doc_friction.issue: allocate.py's buildable hint 'Bayer: per-pixel Laplacian weight' gave no hint the earlier held-out frames had already been used once; a fresh held-out set had to be found by listing the sample repo.
Background subshell `(mkdir X && cd X ...) & cd X` raced; harmless, but the cloud-session notes could suggest creating scratch dirs before backgrounding.

deviations.why: The landed slice is an opt-in algorithm option plus a negative result, not a new default: the per-sensel weight lost luma on the finest held-out frames.
deviations.did: Shipped laplace='adaptive' as an option, kept 3/16 default, and added a fresh 5-frame held-out set (A7 IV, D800E, 7D, GF7, NX1) to give an uncontaminated test.
deviations.result: Fresh set: adaptive +0.10 dB colour on average (4 of 5 better); the shipped 3/16 default beat all seven LibRaw methods on all five fresh frames.

goal: Close the Bayer luma gap on fine aliased frames with a per-sensel Laplacian weight.
notes: Tuning on 70D/D810/sheet: least-squares second-difference weight, 3x3, clipped [1/8,1/4], colour sum 146.59 vs 145.75 for 3/16. First held-out (A7 III, E-M10, K-1 II): -0.08/+0.02/-0.04 colour, A7 III luma -0.33. Oracle diagnostic: per-sensel best of 1/8 vs 1/4 has 17-49% less green error, but no tested feature ranks it with a consistent sign (|rho|<=0.16 on real frames). Two other selectors (curvature ratio, beta/16 regression) dropped. Fresh held-out run once. Local checks: photo-editing pytest 1198 passed, 8 skipped (rawpy 0.25 / LibRaw 0.22.2 venv); post front-matter, links and similarity checks clean; flagship validate clean. venture-preflight.mjs photo-editing: clean.
